extraction.name: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context
extraction.description: We present a new dataset with the goal of advancing the state-of-the-art in object recognition by placing the question of object recognition in the context of the broader question of scene understanding.
extraction.creator: Tsung-Yi Lin Michael Maire Serge Belongie Lubomir Bourdev Ross Girshick James Hays Pietro Perona Deva Ramanan C. Lawrence Zitnick Piotr Doll ´ar
extraction.rai:dataCollection: First and most importantly, we harvested a large set of images containing contextual relationships and noniconic object views. We accomplished this using a surprisingly simple yet effective technique that queries for pairs of objects in conjunction with images retrieved via scene-based queries
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We took care to minimize the chance of near-duplicate images existing across splits by explicitly removing near duplicates (detected with [43]) and grouping images by photographer and date taken.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Our annotation pipeline is split into 3 primary tasks: (a) labeling the categories present in the image ( x4.1), (b) locating and marking all instances of the labeled categories ( x4.2), and (c) segmenting each object instance ( x4.3).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Object category presence is often ambiguous. Indeed as Fig. 4(a) indicates, even dedicated experts often disagree on object presence, e.g. due to inherent ambiguity in the image or disagreement about category definitions.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: To accommodate a faster release schedule, we split the MS COCO dataset into two roughly equal parts. The first half of the dataset was released in 2014, the second half will be released in 2015.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: We currently only label “things”, but labeling “stuff” may also provide significant contextual information that may be useful for detection.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: MS COCO is designed for the detection and segmentation of objects occurring in their natural context.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: First and most importantly, we harvested a large set of images containing contextual relationships and noniconic object views. rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: we collected images from Flickr which tends to have fewer iconic images.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: we collected images from Flickr which tends to have fewer iconic images. Flickr contains photos uploaded by amateur photographers with searchable metadata and keywords.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We took care to minimize the chance of near-duplicate images existing across splits by explicitly removing near duplicates (detected with [43]) and grouping images by photographer and date taken.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Our annotation pipeline is split into 3 primary tasks: (a) labeling the categories present in the image ( x4.1), (b) locating and marking all instances of the labeled categories ( x4.2), and (c) segmenting each object instance ( x4.3).

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: For all crowdsourcing tasks we used workers on Amazon’s Mechanical Turk (AMT).

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Object category presence is often ambiguous. Indeed as Fig. 4(a) indicates, even dedicated experts often disagree on object presence, e.g. due to inherent ambiguity in the image or disagreement about category definitions.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: To ensure high recall, 8 workers were asked to label each image.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We modified source code from the OpenSurfaces project [16], which defines a single AMT task for segmenting multiple regions of a homogenous material in real-scenes.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: To accommodate a faster release schedule, we split the MS COCO dataset into two roughly equal parts. The first half of the dataset was released in 2014, the second half will be released in 2015.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We currently only label “things”, but labeling “stuff” may also provide significant contextual information that may be useful for detection.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: MS COCO is designed for the detection and segmentation of objects occurring in their natural context.
